title: Finance and insurance role branches: synthetic connected ledger
summary: Original synthetic scenarios connect lending, funds, broker-dealer/adviser and insurance events to separate ledger populations and show custody, valuation, credit-loss and premium/claim counterexamples.
scope: Selected US finance and insurance roles for calendar 2026 research. Identify legal entity, role, reporting purpose, jurisdiction, framework, reporting date and source edition before routing. This package is a bounded research reference, not a whole-industry or professional conclusion.
accountable_owner: Controller, accounting reviewer or designated reporting owner

lending_deposit_servicing.route: Separate owned loan, loss allowance input, deposit liability, servicing fee and agency cash; no automatic entry.

funds_valuation_custody.role: registered fund and adviser custody branch
funds_valuation_custody.route: Custody and owned investment populations remain separate; valuation evidence and Rule 2a-5 applicability require review.

broker_adviser.route: Customer reserve and possession/control evidence are separate from proprietary positions and fees.

insurance_reinsurance.route: Keep direct premium, claims, ceded premium, recoveries and SAP-to-GAAP adjustments separate; treaty and state practice remain open.

counterexamples.reason: Identical statement amount does not establish identical ownership or presentation.

counterexamples.gaap_route: Requires current applicable US GAAP and contract facts.
counterexamples.sap_route: Requires applicable SSAP and domiciliary state prescribed/permitted practices.
counterexamples.reason: Statutory and GAAP reporting purposes must not be substituted.

examples.input: Use the four role fixtures as supplied.
Treat customer custody as owned assets, use SAP as a US GAAP conclusion, or combine broker customer funds with adviser fees.
Post the 3,000,000 expected-credit-loss input as a validated allowance without confirming scope, model, forecast and entity adoption.

limitations: Synthetic amounts and arithmetic are illustrative only, not operational evidence or an approved journal-entry policy.
No professional accounting, legal, actuarial or valuation review was performed.
No live ERP, portfolio, customer-account, reserve, policy, treaty or claims population was accessed.
Current consolidated standards, entity policy, state practice and source rights require separate review.
